# Exterior minima for all units of a splitting field and for the subgroup generated by its roots

The author-side researcher for [G0001](../tasks/Yin_T_G0001_v1.md#contract) developed the ambient minimum, the relative norm test and the separating tower below.
The root-generated minimum and the signed-product measure estimate come from [C345v304](Yin_C_G0345_v304.md#statement).

<a id="statement"></a>
## Ambient units, the transfer test and the size of the separation

Let \(F\subset\mathbb C\) be finite and Galois over \(\mathbb Q\), with group \(G\) and complex conjugation \(\tau\).
For a subgroup \(A\) of the algebraic units, write \(\widetilde A=\{y:y^N\in\mu_\infty A \text{ for some }N\ge1\}\).
For a reciprocal nontorsion unit \(y\), let \(b(y)\) count the distinct conjugates of \(y\) of modulus greater than one.
For \(J\le G\) and a nontrivial homomorphism \(\lambda:J\to\{1,-1\}\), put
\[
 c(J,\lambda)=\#\{gJ\in G/J:g^{-1}\tau g\notin\lambda^{-1}(-1)\}.
\]
Then
\[
 \min_{\substack{y\in\widetilde{\mathcal O_F^\times}\\
             y\ {\rm reciprocal,\ nontorsion}}}b(y)
       =\min_{\substack{(J,\lambda)\\c(J,\lambda)>0}}c(J,\lambda).       \tag{1}
\]
The empty minimum is \(+\infty\), and every finite minimum on the left is attained in \(\mathcal O_F^\times\).

The ambient field has a one-exterior unit precisely when it contains a quadratic extension \(L/K\) with \(K\) totally real and exactly one real place of \(K\) splitting into two real places of \(L\).
For such \(L/K\), every nontorsion relative norm-one unit generates \(L\) over \(\mathbb Q\).
Up to conjugation and rational sign it is a Salem number if \([K:\mathbb Q]\ge2\), and a reciprocal quadratic unit otherwise.
For a reciprocal irreducible input with splitting field \(F\), the [relative norm test](#transfer) decides whether its roots generate this particular rank-one group up to saturation.
When the test succeeds, a signed subset product in this same \(L\) has measure at most that of the input.

For each \(q=3^n,\ n\ge1\), there is a monic irreducible reciprocal \(P_n\in\mathbb Z[X]\) of degree \(4q\) such that its splitting field contains a fixed quartic Salem number and
\[
 \min_{\substack{y\in\widetilde{\Gamma_n}\\
       y\ {\rm reciprocal,\ nontorsion}}} b(y)=q,\qquad
 \log M(P_n)\ \ge\ \frac{q}{11}\log(43/2),                              \tag{2}
\]
where \(\Gamma_n\) is the subgroup generated by the roots of \(P_n\).
The original roots attain this minimum.
Thus the ambient minimum can be one while the root-generated minimum grows without bound, and these inputs themselves have growing total measure.

<a id="ambient"></a>
## Relative unit ranks count the admissible ambient pairs

Fix \(J,\lambda\), let \(H=\ker\lambda\), and put \(K=F^J,\ L=F^H\).
Then \(L/K\) is quadratic.
Classify the cosets of \(J\) fixed by \(\tau\) according to the sign \(\lambda(g^{-1}\tau g)\).
Write \(f_+,f_-\) for the respective numbers of fixed cosets of positive and negative sign, and let \(k\) count the two-cycles.
Thus \(c(J,\lambda)=f_++2k\).
The embeddings of \(K\) correspond to \(G/J\), and each has two lifts corresponding to \(G/H\).
Over a positive fixed coset both lifts are real, over a negative fixed coset the lifts form one complex pair, and each two-cycle gives two complex pairs.
The signatures of \(K,L\) are consequently \((f_++f_-,k)\) and \((2f_+,f_-+2k)\).
The norm on units has image containing the squares of \(\mathcal O_K^\times\).
By the [unit theorem in arbitrary signature](../audits/literature/Con26/Yin_U002.md#con26-u002), the kernel has rank
\[
                (2f_++f_-+2k-1)-(f_++f_-+k-1)=f_++k.                    \tag{3}
\]
This rank is positive exactly when \(c(J,\lambda)>0\).

When positive, choose a nontorsion unit \(a\in L\) of relative norm one.
The nonidentity \(K\)-automorphism of \(L\) takes \(a\) to \(a^{-1}\), so its conjugates are inverse-closed.
All embeddings above the \(f_-\) negative cosets give pairs on the unit circle, by complex conjugation and the norm equation.
The remaining cosets each contribute at most one distinct exterior conjugate, giving \(b(a)\le c(J,\lambda)\).

Conversely, clear a radical exponent and torsion from a reciprocal nontorsion \(y\) by choosing \(w=y^N\in\mathcal O_F^\times\).
The conjugates of \(w\) are inverse-closed.
For \(v=[w]\) in \(\mathcal O_F^\times\otimes_\mathbb Z\mathbb Q\), take \(J\) to be the stabilizer of \(\{v,-v\}\) and \(\lambda\) its sign action.
Inversion of \(w\) by some element of \(G\) makes the sign nontrivial.
As in the [unit-circle and orbit calculation](Yin_C_G0345_v304.md#lower), \(|gw|=1\) holds exactly when \(\tau gv=-gv\), since \(gw\,\overline{gw}\) is positive real and is torsion exactly when it is one.
The cosets of \(J\) index distinct class pairs, both signs occur among the actual conjugates, and each nonneutral class pair gives an exterior conjugate.
Some pair is nonneutral because \(w\) is a nontorsion unit.
Consequently \(0<c(J,\lambda)\le b(w)\le b(y)\), where the last inequality follows by lifting each distinct exterior power to an exterior conjugate.
Together with (3) and the norm-one construction this proves (1), including the empty case.

<a id="transfer"></a>
## The norm test for a specified Salem subfield

Cost one in (1) requires \(k=0,\ f_+=1\), which is exactly the asserted quadratic extension of a totally real field.
Conversely any such \(L/K\) in \(F\) arises from \(J=\operatorname{Gal}(F/K)\) and its quotient \(\operatorname{Gal}(L/K)\) of order two.
A nontorsion relative norm-one unit \(\beta\) has exactly one exterior value among all embeddings of \(L\), counted with multiplicity.
Indeed the two real embeddings over the distinguished place give distinct real reciprocals different from \(\pm1\), while all remaining pairs have modulus one.
Its exterior conjugate occurs \([L:\mathbb Q(\beta)]\) times in that list, so \(\mathbb Q(\beta)=L\).
The same argument applies to every positive power of \(\beta\).
More generally, if a reciprocal one-exterior unit has any positive power in \(F\), then it already belongs to \(F\): its unique exterior conjugate maps to the unique exterior value under powering, with exactly one preimage among its conjugates, so powering preserves its degree and field.
For genuine Salem numbers, Smyth records Salem's power-degree theorem and gives the stronger fixed-field statement that each Salem number in a field generated by a Salem number generates that field. [Lemma 2 and Proposition 3](../audits/literature/Smy15/Yin_U001.md#smy15-u001)

Let \(P\) be monic irreducible reciprocal with nontorsion unit roots and splitting field \(F\), and let \(\Gamma\) be generated by those roots.
Fix such a field \(L/K\), write \(\iota\) for its nontrivial automorphism over \(K\), and choose a nontorsion relative norm-one unit \(\beta\in L\).
Then
\[
 \beta\in\widetilde\Gamma
 \ \Longleftrightarrow\
 \frac{N_{F/L}(x)}{\iota N_{F/L}(x)}\ \text{is nontorsion for some root }x\text{ of }P.   \tag{4}
\]
Every displayed ratio is a relative norm-one unit of \(L\) and belongs to \(\Gamma\), since \(\iota\) lifts to \(G\).
If one is nontorsion, rank one in (3) gives a nonzero power of \(\beta\) equal up to torsion to a power of the ratio.
Conversely, on the rational unit space use \(D=(1-s)\sum_{h\in H}h\), with \(H=\operatorname{Gal}(F/L)\) and \(s\) a lift of \(\iota\).
It sends \([x]\) to the class of the ratio in (4) and sends \([\beta]\) to \(2|H|[\beta]\ne0\).
If \(\beta\in\widetilde\Gamma\), its class is in the rational span of the root classes, so some \(D[x]\) is nonzero.
Here \(D\) is the unnormalized signed average for \(J=\operatorname{Gal}(F/K)\).
The [single-coordinate averaging construction](Yin_C_G0345_v304.md#average) therefore produces a nontorsion signed subset product fixed by \(H\) and inverted by \(s\).
It lies in \(L\), has relative norm one and one exterior conjugate, and its [measure bound](Yin_C_G0345_v304.md#measure) is \(M(P)\).
One can test (4) by factoring \(P\) over \(L\).
If \(f\in L[X]\) is the monic irreducible factor with root \(x\), then \(N_{F/L}(x)=((-1)^{\deg f} f(0))^{[F:L(x)]}\).
The only roots of unity in \(L\) are \(\pm1\), by its real embedding.
Thus (4) holds exactly when some such factor satisfies \(f(0)\ne\pm\iota(f(0))\).

<a id="tower"></a>
## Quartic Salem field and norm-one units of degree \(4q\)

Take the exterior root \(\alpha>1\) of \(X^4-X^3-X^2-X+1\).
The two traces \(t_1,t_2=(1\pm\sqrt{13})/2\) satisfy \(t^2-t-3=0\), with \(t_1>2\) and \(-2<t_2<2\).
In \(B=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{13})\), the two elements \(d_i=t_i^2-4\) have opposite signs at one embedding and interchange signs at the other.
Neither \(d_i\) nor \(d_1d_2\) is a square in \(B\), since each is negative at some real embedding.
The splitting field \(F_0=B(\sqrt{d_1},\sqrt{d_2})\) has degree eight, and its action on the two inverse pairs realizes the full signed permutation group \(D_4\) of order eight.
Indeed its injection into that group is faithful and both groups have order eight.
In particular the polynomial is irreducible, \(\alpha\) is a quartic Salem number, and \(A=\mathbb Q(\alpha)\) is quadratic over \(B\), of signature \((2,1)\).
The central element \(z\) of order two in \(D_4\) inverts both root pairs and restricts to the nontrivial automorphism of \(A/B\).

Let \(K_n=\mathbb Q(\zeta_{3^{n+1}})^+\) for \(n\ge0\), where the superscript denotes the maximal real subfield.
This is a nested tower with \(K_0=\mathbb Q\) and cyclic group \(H_n\) of order \(3^n\): the residue classes congruent to one modulo three give representatives modulo sign, and \(4\) generates them because \(v_3(4^{3^j}-1)=j+1\) by cubing and induction.
Write \(q=3^n\), with \(n\ge1\), and \(F_n=F_0K_n\).
The coprime Galois degrees give \(\operatorname{Gal}(F_n/\mathbb Q)=D_4\times H_n\).
Define \(A_n=AK_n,\ B_n=BK_n\).
Their signatures are \((2q,q)\) and \((2q,0)\), as each embedding of \(A\) or \(B\) combines independently with each real embedding of \(K_n\).
The relative norm-one group \(U_n=\ker(N_{A_n/B_n}:\mathcal O_{A_n}^\times\to\mathcal O_{B_n}^\times)\) has rank \(q\) by the same square-image and unit-rank calculation as (3).
Define \(U_0\) likewise, of rank one.
The norm to \(A_{n-1}\) maps \(U_n\) into \(U_{n-1}\) because the cubic and quadratic norm products commute.
Its kernel thus has rank at least \(q-q/3>0\).
Choose any nontorsion unit \(u\) in this kernel and let \(P_n\) be its minimal polynomial.

Let \(h\) generate the subgroup of order three of \(H_n\).
Since \(u\,h(u)\,h^2(u)=1\), the operator \(1+h+h^2\) vanishes on the rational span \(V\) of all conjugate classes of \(u\), by centrality.
Thus no nonidentity element of \(H_n\) fixes a nonzero vector of \(V\): some power of that element generates the order-three subgroup, whose fixed vectors would satisfy \(3v=0\).
If \((d,a)\in D_4\times H_n\) fixes \(u\), its fourth power fixes \([u]\).
As \(d^4=1\) and \(q\) is odd, this forces \(a=1\).
The stabilizer of \(u\) therefore lies in \(D_4\) and contains the order-two subgroup fixing \(A\).
It excludes \(z\), since \(z(u)=u^{-1}\ne u\).
Every subgroup of \(D_4\) of order at least four contains \(z\): a rotation of order four squares to \(z\), and two distinct reflections multiply to a nontrivial rotation.
Hence the stabilizer has exactly order two and \(\deg u=4q\), so \(\mathbb Q(u)=A_n\).
The normal closure of \(A_n\) is \(F_n\), as its conjugates contain all conjugates of \(A\) as well as \(K_n\).
This proves that \(\alpha\) belongs to the actual splitting field of \(P_n\).

All embeddings above the real-split place of \(B\), combined with the \(q\) embeddings of \(K_n\), give \(q\) pairs of real reciprocal conjugates of \(u\).
Each has exactly one exterior member since \(u\) is nontorsion.
Above the other \(q\) places of \(B_n\), complex conjugation induces the quadratic automorphism, and the norm condition makes both roots in each pair neutral.
Therefore \(P_n\) is monic irreducible reciprocal with exactly \(q\) exterior roots.

<a id="radicals"></a>
## Every reciprocal root-generated radical has at least \(q\) exterior conjugates

Let \(y\in\widetilde{\Gamma_n}\) be reciprocal and nontorsion and choose \(w=y^N\in\Gamma_n\).
Its conjugates are inverse-closed and every conjugate has nonzero class in \(V\).
The central cyclic \(H_n\) acts on the actual unordered inverse pairs of these conjugates.
This action is free: if \(a\in H_n\) fixes a pair, then \(a^2\) fixes its class, forcing \(a^2=1\) by the norm relation on \(V\), and \(q\) is odd.
The action preserves the set of neutral pairs because it commutes with \(\tau\), and neutrality of a class \(v\) is equivalent to \((1+\tau)v=0\).
Hence its orbits on the nonneutral pairs all have size \(q\).
Every nonneutral pair contributes exactly one exterior conjugate, so \(b(w)\) is a positive multiple of \(q\).
Lifting exterior conjugates through the positive power gives \(b(y)\ge b(w)\ge q\), and \(u\) realizes equality.

<a id="example"></a>
## An explicit degree-twelve input

At \(q=3\) put \(t=\zeta_9+\zeta_9^{-1}\), so \(t^3-3t+1=0\), and choose the generator \(h\) acting by \(h(t)=t^2-2\).
Set \(\eta=\alpha+t-1\) and \(u=\eta\,zh(\eta)/(z(\eta)\,h(\eta))\).
The two commuting automorphisms \(z,h\) give \(z(u)=u^{-1}\) and \(u\,h(u)\,h^2(u)=1\).
The following resultant also verifies the nonzero denominator and shows directly that \(u\) is a unit.
With \(p=x^4-x^3-x^2-x+1\), set
\[
 A=(x+t-1)(1+x(t^2-3)),\qquad B=(1+x(t-1))(x+t^2-3).
\]
Eliminating \(t\) and then \(x\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{Res}_x\bigl(p,\operatorname{Res}_t(t^3-3t+1,BY-A)\bigr)=81Q(Y),
\]
where
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 Q(Y)={}&Y^{12}+33Y^{11}+75Y^{10}-841Y^9-153Y^8-441Y^7+465Y^6\\
        &-441Y^5-153Y^4-841Y^3+75Y^2+33Y+1 .
 \end{aligned}
\]
The leading coefficient \(81\) in the elimination gives the nonzero norm of \(B\), and \(u=A(\alpha,t)/B(\alpha,t)\).
It is a real root of the monic unit polynomial \(Q\), with \(Q(1)=-2187\) and \(Q(-1)=2809\), so it is nontorsion.
The preceding degree proof now shows that \(Q\) is its minimal polynomial.
Consequently this explicit input has three exterior roots, exact radical minimum three and a quartic Salem number in its splitting field.

<a id="price"></a>
## An explicit measure bound throughout the tower

Modulo 43 the quartic polynomial of \(\alpha\) has four distinct roots \(3,17,29,38\).
[Simple-root lifting](../audits/literature/Con26e/Yin_U001.md#con26e-u001) gives its full splitting over \(\mathbb Q_{43}\).
The cyclotomic field of \(3\)-power conductor is unramified at 43, since the roots of its defining unity equation have distinct reductions and all lift from a finite residue extension.
Thus 43 is unramified in \(F_n\) and its Frobenius elements restrict trivially to \(F_0\).
They belong to the central factor \(H_n\), so all primes above 43 have the same Frobenius element \(\sigma\).
In particular \(a^{43}-\sigma(a)\in43\mathcal O_{F_n}\) for every integral \(a\), by the residue congruences and unramified factorization of 43.
For any nontorsion unit \(a\) this difference is nonzero, since equality would give \(a^{43^j}=a\) for \(j=\operatorname{ord}(\sigma)\).
Let \(d=[F_n:\mathbb Q]\) and \(h(a)=d^{-1}\sum_g\log\max(1,|ga|)\).
Taking absolute norms and bounding each complex difference by \(2\max(1,|ga|)^{43}\max(1,|g\sigma a|)\) gives
\[
       43^d\le |N_{F_n/\mathbb Q}(a^{43}-\sigma a)|
              \le 2^d\exp(44d\,h(a)).
\]
Thus \(h(a)\ge\log(43/2)/44\).
Since \(\deg u=4q\) and \(u\) is a unit, \(\log M(P_n)=4q h(u)\), which proves the measure estimate in (2).
Amoroso and Dvornicich use this Frobenius comparison to obtain \(h(a)\ge\log(p/2)/(p+1)\) for nontorsion \(a\in\mathbb Q(\zeta_m)^\times\) when \(m\ge3\), \(m\not\equiv2\pmod4\) and \(p\ge3\) is a prime not dividing \(m\). [Lemma 2 and Proposition 1](../audits/literature/AD00/Yin_U001.md#ad00-u001)
The qualitative uniform height bound also follows from Amoroso, David and Zannier's central-extension theorem with fixed field \(F_0\), whose completion at 43 is \(\mathbb Q_{43}\). [Application of Proposition 4.2 to such composita](../audits/literature/ADZ14/Yin_U001.md#abelian-split-compositum-application)
The separation refutes a transfer from ambient field membership alone for unrestricted inputs.
A bounded root-generated exterior count for inputs of arbitrarily small positive total measure, or a uniform gap for inputs resisting such a reduction, remains open.
